# Star-orbit realistic planet textures
Author: Solar System Scope / INOVE
Source: https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/
License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Downloaded 2026-10-11, original 2048 x 1024 JPEG maps, without resizing.
Files: https://www.solarsystemscope.com/textures/download/2k_{name}.jpg
Names: sun, mercury, venus_atmosphere, earth_daymap, mars, jupiter, saturn, uranus, neptune.
These maps combine space imagery and artistic reconstruction; they are not unmodified photographs. Venus uses its atmosphere map.
Used only for the star-orbit realistic display style. Shader applies existing spin axes, rotation phases and directional lighting. World physics are unchanged.

## Satellite surface maps (2026-10-11)
Current displayed satellites each use their own map, distributed by CelestiaContent:
https://github.com/CelestiaProject/CelestiaContent
See satellite-sources.json for pinned original URLs and per-file licenses;
SATELLITE-CREDITS.txt contains the complete upstream author/data credits.
Individual *.license files retain attribution and CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0 terms;
unannotated maps retain the upstream GPL-2.0-or-later distribution terms, included
in GPL-2.0-or-later.txt and SATELLITE-LICENSE.md. These are separate image assets.
Original maps are retained without rescaling or fabricated detail. Most maps are
2048 or 4096 pixels wide. Proteus is 1024 pixels wide; spacecraft coverage and
resolution vary, and mosaics include reconstructed or interpolated gaps.
Only realistic satellite appearance changes; orbital dynamics and display sizes
are unchanged. The shader adds solar lighting and an orbit-aligned synchronous
surface orientation, not a claim of exact cartographic ephemeris orientation.
